newsitem.title: USA: US Congress negotiators cut FY97 EEP to $10 Mln.
newsitem.headline: US Congress negotiators cut FY97 EEP to $10 Mln.

text.p: A team of House and Senate negotiators tentatively agreed Wednesday to reduce funding for the major U.S. ag export subsidy program to $10 million in fiscal 1997.

Congress originally alloted $100 million for the Export Enhancement Program. However, the House passed a bill last week to reduce funding to $10 million. The Senate version of the emergency spending bill allowed $50 million.
During a session Wednesday to draft a final version of the bill, senators agreed to accept the House's spending level.
Analysts said the reduction would have little impact since the United States has not subsidized a grain sale in nearly two years.

The House and Senate also wanted to reduce funding for U.S. export credit guarantees to $3.5 billion this fiscal year, a $2 billion cut. Use of the credits has been low, lawmakers said, so it was proper to adjust the ceiling on expenditures.
